attempts.why: Use :nth-child(odd of :not([hidden])) so hidden display:none rows are not counted in striped parity, fixing shifted tinting.

selfVerify.reason: Striping parity is now correct and hidden-aware: r1 (1st visible) tinted rgba(111,120,135,0.04), hidden tr[hidden] is display:none 0x0 and not counted, r2 (2nd visible) white, r3 tinted, r4 white – alternating as required by :nth-child(odd of :not([hidden])). Bug pattern of r1+r2 both tinted / r3+r4 inverted is gone, no other breakage.

pick.suspected: Striped table uses :nth-child(even/odd) on tbody tr / td to apply the alternating background. :nth-child counts all children including tr[hidden] (display:none), so the hidden row shifts the parity: r1 and r2 both get the tinted rgba(111,120,135,0.04) background and r3/r4 are inverted. Should use a hidden-aware striping selector (e.g. not counting [hidden] rows) or :nth-of-type with :not([hidden]) logic.
